name: Developer assembling a personal job-search automation

context.occupation: Software developer building personal search tooling
context.seniority: Technically experienced; desired job seniority unspecified
context.employment_state: Exploring jobs while building a reusable personal workflow
constraints: Wants programmatic search and career-page monitoring
Needs stable IDs and incremental updates
API/MCP documentation matters more than a polished dashboard
context.company_awareness: Has a target list and can identify ATS providers, but wants to reduce scraper maintenance.

trigger: A hand-written career-page checker breaks after a site redesign, prompting a search for maintained APIs or an MCP server that can plug into a personal assistant.

searches_run.query: job search API MCP server open source
searches_run.observation: Retrieved several GitHub projects offering MCP job-search interfaces, including self-hosted tools and provider-connected adapters. A source-code repository is a competing implementation path, not evidence of willingness to buy a jobseeker subscription.

searches_run.query: open source monitor company careers pages new jobs alerts personal automation
searches_run.observation: Retrieved a self-hosted ATS polling project, a managed alert service and generic page-monitoring guidance. Direct inspection of job-alerts documents title/location filters, known-job state, configurable company registry and SMTP setup.

sources.title: jobsearch-mcp | TadMSTR on GitHub
sources.supports: Retrieved repository advertises self-hosted MCP job search and lists API data providers; runtime behavior not tested.

sources.title: Jobo jobs MCP server | JoboAI on GitHub
sources.supports: Retrieved repository describes structured search tools and provider authentication. Direct page opened, but no integration test or licensing assessment performed.

sources.title: job-alerts | SirFuzzyWalls on GitHub
sources.supports: Directly inspected README describes ATS polling, configurable employers and title/location filters, state retention, local dashboard and SMTP requirements; GitHub shows AGPL-3.0 code license, not data redistribution rights.

sources.title: FirstPost personalised job alerts
sources.supports: Retrieved service description offers monitored career-page alerts, illustrating a managed alternative to self-hosting; claims not tested.

sources.title: Job Seek MCP server README — repository evidence verified by parent agent
sources.supports: Documents hosted https://jseek.co/mcp without authentication, local @jseek/mcp-server package and search_jobs/get_job_detail/search_companies/list_taxonomies/resolve_slugs/create_watchlist_link. Parent also verified /openapi.json redirects to /api/openapi.json. This is repository evidence, not a third external search.

best_entry_page.promise: Document how to use the existing hosted MCP endpoint or local package to search jobs and companies, inspect details and create watchlist links for personal workflows.
best_entry_page.cta: Read the MCP setup guide and try a documented search; use create_watchlist_link to continue into a saved-search flow.
proof_needed: Publish accurate hosted/local setup and tool examples
Document operational limits and expected freshness without inventing guarantees
State permitted personal use and commercial redistribution terms separately
Validate examples against the running endpoint
Measure developer activation separately from paid jobseeker conversion

conversion_objections: Will the documented endpoint remain stable for a personal workflow?
I can self-host a basic company watcher.
I need stable identifiers and clear update/deletion semantics.
Does Pro change API usage or only description filtering? Do not assume the former.
A working MCP interface does not establish commercial redistribution rights.

avoid_targeting.query: free unlimited job postings API commercial redistribution
avoid_targeting.reason: No unlimited-service promise or commercial data rights are established.
Auto-apply is not among the verified tools and is a different intent.

message_to_founder: Simulation: Your existing MCP interface could save me scraper maintenance, so clear examples and predictable limits matter. I may use it for a personal assistant and later adopt managed alerts, but developer activation should not be counted as demand for a paid jobseeker plan without evidence.

confidence_and_limits: Synthetic simulation, not an interview or an independent respondent. Two queries retrieved on 2026-09-28, with at least one direct page inspection. Queries without observed source IDs are hypotheses. Combined retrieval is not a controlled ranking report. No volume, difficulty or conversion inference. Source claims and role availability can change; product fit uses the supplied repository brief. Correction based on parent-verified repository evidence: the product already has hosted MCP, a local MCP package and public OpenAPI endpoints. Developer-doc acquisition is legitimate and separate from paid jobseeker intent. Public mcp.json is intentionally 404 and is not cited as discovery. Operational limits, commercial data rights and conversion remain unverified. The two external searches are unchanged.
